critical_issues.msg: logout endpoint has no auth dependency — any party with the HttpOnly cookie can call it, enabling denial-of-service logout or user coercion without any credentials.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add current_user: AuthContext = Depends(get_current_user) to the logout signature, consistent with logout_all.

critical_issues.msg: `location` parameter is accepted but never used — geo-change detection is unimplemented (rule 111: hidden coupling).
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove `location` from the signature if geo-change detection is not implemented, or add the comparison: after the IP check, add `if location and device.last_location and location != device.last_location: reasons.append(SuspiciousActivityReason.GEO_CHANGE)`.

critical_issues.msg: finish_registration accepts any origin from the client without validating it matches rp_id — a malicious client could register with an arbitrary origin.
critical_issues.suggestion: Validate that origin is https and matches the expected rp_id (e.g., origin must be https://<rp_id> or https://<rp_id>:<port>). Remove the TODO comment and add actual validation.

critical_issues.msg: verify_assertion accepts any origin without validation — same attack surface as finish_registration.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add origin validation matching the expected rp_id before accepting the assertion.

suggestions.msg: transports column uses sa.String(length=100) but JSON-encoded transport arrays (e.g. '["usb","nfc","ble","internal"]') regularly exceed 100 chars.
suggestions.suggestion: Change sa.String(length=100) to sa.Text() or sa.String(length=255) for the transports column.

suggestions.msg: ix_device_trust_user_id indexes user_id but not the frequently-used WHERE clause pair (user_id, trusted), and device_trust has no unique constraint on (user_id, device_fingerprint), allowing duplicate fingerprints for the same user.
suggestions.suggestion: Consider a composite unique constraint on (user_id, device_fingerprint) in device_trust, or at minimum add a covering index including trusted for efficient lookups.

suggestions.msg: rotate_refresh_token truncates remaining TTL to whole days — a user with 8 days left gets 8 days on rotation, preserving most of the original window, but the logic could be clearer.

suggestions.msg: verify_access_token swallows jwt.ExpiredSignatureError and jwt.InvalidTokenError identically, returning None — this is safe but makes debugging harder.
suggestions.suggestion: Log (but not expose) the specific failure reason for operational visibility without changing behavior.

suggestions.msg: Bare except: clause silently falls back to using the raw attestation object string as the public key — this could store an unusable credential without any error signal.
suggestions.suggestion: Catch specific exceptions (base64.b64decode.DecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) and raise ValidationException; only fallback for known-safe formats.

suggestions.msg: Bare except: clause silently ignores all exceptions in sign count parsing — parsing errors are invisible and sign_count stays 0.
suggestions.suggestion: Catch specific exceptions (ValueError, IndexError, struct.error) and handle them explicitly rather than using a bare except.

suggestions.msg: Sign count byte offset (37) and length (4) are magic numbers — the structure is documented only in a comment.
suggestions.suggestion: Define named constants (AUTHENTICATOR_DATA_SIGN_COUNT_OFFSET, AUTHENTICATOR_DATA_SIGN_COUNT_LENGTH) or parse from a structured AuthenticatorData class.

suggestions.msg: _consume_challenge is not atomic — concurrent requests could consume the same challenge between the SELECT and the consume update within a single request.
suggestions.suggestion: Use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE consumed=False RETURNING to eliminate the race window.

suggestions.msg: The 256-byte threshold for choosing decode_credential_id vs base64.b64decode is arbitrary and undocumented — unclear why 256 bytes distinguishes the encoding scheme.
suggestions.suggestion: Document the threshold rationale or refactor to always attempt url-safe decode first, then fallback to standard base64.
